item.title: Re: Deletions 70: If the fact will not fit the theory – let the theory go.
item.content:encoded:
SCP-5334 is a 8 feet long, 1 foot wide, and 2 feet, 6 inches tall Chilopoda. SCP-5334's body segments are covered in a thick shell, with dark brown stripes covering the black shell. Protruding from the shells are 2 feet tall horns, which are used as a defense mechanism. A pair of legs appear on every body segment. SCP-5334 has around 173 body segments. SCP-5334's head is an inch longer than its body segments, and contains a horn at the tip of its head. The horn is a inch larger than the previous horns. Two 1 foot antennae protrude from the face of SCP-5334 as well in back end. Two pincers, 1 foot and 8 inches each, are attached to SCP-5334's head, which are used to grab and crush prey.

Deleted at -15 and three votes.

item.title: SCP Idea: Cogito, Ergo Sum
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Psychological

Page Layout (Optional): Interview articles, "Sit-in Classes"

Elevator Pitch: Students who want college credit attend a class taught by an unusual professor.

Central Narrative: Letters from "South Euton University" are sent out to high school and college students who want college credit. The class being taught is labeled "Philosophy of Existence," and is taught by Professor Phillip Oliver Zofia. The classroom has an unusual setup, with strange posters and maps that have countries improperly labeled. Above the whiteboard is a large poster, upon which is written, "Cogito, Ergo Sum." The professor himself is a man described as "gaunt," "faint," even "ethereal."

+ show block
– hide block

The class begins with the professor providing the students with an initial quiz. The questions are very easy (2+2=?), but the students fail when they provide standard answers. The professor then proceeds to teach the class, telling them blatantly incorrect answers, and then testing them on the incorrect knowledge. Those that refuse to answer "properly" are given personal instruction by Dr. Zofia. The sessions apparently take half an hour, though one student describes it feeling as though she was in there for days (vague as to whether she was or not). Invariably, the students start giving him the answers he wants, whether through exasperation or actually starting to buy into his teaching. They become increasingly suggestible as this goes on. Simultaneously, Dr. Zofia grows stronger, fuller, more substantial.

The final test consists of a piece of paper, asking, "Cogito, ergo sum. Concur?" There is also a line where the students write their names, which they invariably do. At the conclusion of the test, the students disappear, while Dr. Zofia seems to become completely rejuvenated. The SCP agent monitoring this situation (implied that Zofia is amused by their presence and is toying with them) offers them a letter and an invitation to join them next semester, and then is ushered out.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Aside from the oddities of the classroom, the central question, "I think, therefore I am," is explored. If one stops thinking, do they really exist? And if one's thoughts supercede another's, does that not make them more you, than you? This is also meant to be mild commentary on the education system caring more about correct answers than understanding material.

Additional Notes:

item.title: JS Staff Post -- Forum Crit -- Info
item.content:encoded:
Author,

Per the required reading forum guidelines, please fill out the concept template to seek feedback on your idea:

 **Seeking Greenlights:** Put yes or no. **Page Type:** SCP Article, Tale, GoI Format, Joke SCP, Site Dossier, Other (specify) **Genre (Optional):** Horror, Drama/Emotional, Comedy, Action, History, Other (specify) **Page Layout (Optional):** [How will you will structure the page in terms of information presentation, or plot development? If you plan on using a unique format/format screw, describe that here.] **Elevator Pitch:** [What is the basic core idea? Use a bullet point list if necessary.] **Central Narrative:** [Describe the story beats or overarching context/"big picture" for your piece. If there is no story content, put "none".] **Hook/Attention-Grabber:** [What is novel/unique about your premise? What is special about your idea here that will make it stand out among the other works already on the mainsite?] **Additional Notes:** [Note any concerns or particular areas of assistance you would like reviewers to focus on.]

Rather than posting a new comment, edit your previous post using the "edit" function under the "options" tab to the lower right of your first comment.

Remember that the combined text for your answers to the last four sections (Elevator Pitch, Central Narrative, Hook/Attention-Grabber, and Additional Notes) MAY NOT exceed 400 words. For convenience, authors can use this page to check wordcount: https://wordcounter.net/

Once you have revised your post accordingly, please reach out to reviewers to request that they look at your thread. You can find example lists of contacts in the Required Reading thread linked above.

The fact that the first three sentences already contains major logical and in-universe errors does not fare well to me as a reader. In fact, I have no incentive to continue reading because of these errors. Let me explain:

+ Reveal
- Close

Object Class: Safe

Special Containment Procedures: SCP 5764 is impossible to contain physically, instead, it was convinced by the foundation to stay at Site-43, in a standard cell.

Why is this labeled as Safe? If this entity can pass through any walls and is "impossible to contain," then it should certainly not be classified as "Safe." The only explanation I can think of for this is the insinuation that "Safe" = "Entity is physically harmless" or something to that extent, which is not the Object Classes purpose. This is specified on multiple guides and even the Guide to Newbies, I believe.

His presence is to be monitored constantly, as he roams the site's halls, passing through walls and occasionally slipping into any room imaginable, including another SCP's cell,

What does "any room imaginable" even quantify towards? Why imaginable? This isn't appropriate clinical tone whatsoever. This could've been easily rectified by: "SCP-5764's presence is be continually monitored as it is capable of freely transversing Site-XX with no visible restictions." (<— Although even something like this provides a multitude of logical and in-universe errors. Why is this being allowed? Why hasn't the Foundation moved or convinced the anomaly to be moved towards another secure area? The list goes on)

[…] these accidents only take mere moments to solve however, and no lasting negative effects on the staff or the scps has been detected.

This sentence is complex, choppy, and severely grammatically flawed. This could have been rectified by a simple grammar checker or a reviewer. In fact, most of these errors could have probably been fixed if you had someone else look at it before you posted it.


The fact that this doesn't even bother being logically or grammatically accurate doesn't make me want to read it whatsoever. The anomaly itself is also conceptually weak, constituting towards a pretty lackluster OP entity that I have no interest in due to the aforementioned problems listed above. Next time, I highly suggest you pay attention the the Guides and Essays as well as using the Forums (i.e. the Idea Critique Forum or the Draft Critique Forum) before you publish future articles. I promise, they're there for a reason.

item.title: Re: Sword Ballerina (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Thank you so much for your help! I'll edit the first post with ideas that I had after and before your critics to improve the idea. I have an eight-paged document with ideas for this one, but I've tried to summary everything as I was nervous with the 400 words limit. I'll list above what will be revised.

+ The Concept
- Hide

I've listed everything and will answer your concerns one by one:

  • Protection Directive: This sword was created to be an "Ultimate Weapon" for an "Ultimate Warrior". The protection it gives is based on the question "can my owner defend itself from this attack"? If the answer is "No", it will transform into the automaton to defend it. If it is "Yes", then it will continue as a sword. The system isn't perfect as it can't protect the host from anything non-humanoid (birds, plants, fungi, etc). It is closely connected with the memory keeping, as both the SCP and the owner have to be powerful combatants (see Memory Keeping above).
  • Transformation: the sword is its "dormant" form and the automaton is its "activated" form. It will keep sword form till the "protection directive" is activated. As I forgot to mention, the automaton attacks are always slashing or piercing as a sword, even its punches or kicks. It comes from its references, but has a meaning.
  • Ballet Dancing: That's my fault as I've forgot to mention previous owners. One of its owners was a soviet ballerina that fought in the Russian Civil War. As the ballet is based on perfection (one of the SCP keywords), it blended the dance with its fighting style. It is also a thing that comes from the SCP references.
  • Memory Keeping: The SCP memory keeping is based on maintaining everything that can be used on warfare, mainly languages, martial arts, weapon mastery and other skills. It keeped full memory of its favorite masters (favorite almost meaning "most sanguinary"), including life and murdering scenes. This will be important to the next topic.
  • Host Changing: The only way known to become a host is killing the previous one. If it dies of anything that is not murder, the SCP becomes a violent guard of its previous owner remains. Anyway, non-violent deaths are difficult to achieve, as the host is especially skilled for surviving.
+ Narrative and Hook
- Hide

As both are very close, I'll write about them together, talking about the three hosts.

  1. The first gets the SCP control by accident, as it was an agent from a task force sent to control and retrieve the SCP. By them we first get the SCP idea. Because of its unknown intrusive memories, it gets an mnestics treatment as researchers think this will uncover the SCP's powers and history, but the host ends up having PTSD as it lives through the atrocities the previous host had made, killing another agent during one of its hyperarousal episodes. Without escape, the Foundation choses a new host.
  2. The second one is used to test the SCP protection skills, as they continue unexplained. The researchers discover that it only replies to aggressions where the host is off guard. As the host accepts, they begin a series of tests based on surprise non-lethal ambushes. With the SCP psychic interference, the hosts start presenting paranoid and atypical behavior. As they start getting homicidal, a third host is chosen.
  3. The third is less obvious. It gets special treatment as no one wants another murderous SCP host. They even get a Special Task Force just to protect them from dangers. It's implicit that the third host is treated more as an SCP subject than a human, as even with psychological, therapeutic and psychiatric treatments, the STF commander has the orders to kill them if they get out of control.

I'll try to keep with the "Cold, not Cruel" and "Flawed, not Fools" all the time. I need more critics about it.

item.title: Re: Changing wikidot username
item.content:encoded:
If you've got any pages marked as yours on Attribution Metadata, you'll need to update that page with your new username.

As for Wikidot links… if they're not updated, they won't break immediately - the link will still be there, and it'll still link to your profile page, but it'll still show your old username. However, next time the page is edited, the link will break, and it'll say "user kothardarastrix does not exist." At that point the page will need to be edited manually to update your name to fix it. Sally there's no way of seeing a list of pages that link to your profile, so there no way of knowing for sure all the pages that will break. If you know of any yourself, probably the best bet is to change your name and then update them.

You should know that the user Koth already exists, so if you do choose to change your name, you'll have to pick another.

item.title: SCP Idea - A living Zebra
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: It's a zebra that doesn't die. It doesn't have supernatural resilience, but circumstance always works out in such a way that it survives. If a roof collapses, the portion of roof over the zebra will turn out to be still standing.

Central Narrative: The foundation realizes it's probably a bad idea to fuck with something when it doesn't have to
-The concept is introduced ("lucky zebra"),
-A list of relevant extraordinary circumstances is given
-The last example is enumerated upon:
-Toxins are administered to the horse
-The test is aborted when it almost dies
-It is concluded the horse "accepted" the toxins because we would save it
-Dr.McGuffin proposes injecting it and not saving it
-Because it's just a Zebra, the only way it could survive is by something preventing the staff from injecting toxins
-Testing is suspended

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It's a probability warper that warps around the idea of being a normal zebra. Although it poses no risk of breaching containment, because it's a normal zebra, containment will be breached if that it what's necessary to keep it alive.

Additional Notes: It's written in the vein of many older SCPs: very brief, and more "weird with dangerous implications" than scary

item.title: Re: My Eternal Crusade
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for the review! I really appreciate your honest (if not harsh), critic. I don't think I'm going to abandon this idea entirely just yet, but I will be making some heavy revisions. That said there are a few things I would like to address in your review.

+ show block
– hide block

1) I understand the Foundation isn't interested in killing SCP's. The Crusader would've only be sent out in these "very notable instances". He is an asset to be used, a tool, just like every other SCP with beneficial or valuable anomalies.

2) Yes, The Crusader runs contradictory to the Foundation's motto. That's the idea. The story is about compromise, and how far both sides are willing to compromise. For the Crusader, that is eventually one step farther than he is willing to walk.

3) I never said he was the only anomaly used to hunt, fight, capture, etc other anomalies, or that he was used in all cases. He is a valuable asset to be used in specific cases, and the Foundation is aware of this.

4) His story happens in the past, not the present. He WAS an asset that WAS used until it was proven that he couldn't be trusted (according to Foundation standards anyway). Compromise is the premise, and in the end, the Foundation decides against any further compromise or any compromise at all.

5) I'm not sure what you mean by "deus vult dogwhistling" so feel free to call me unknowledgeable. A quick google search tells me you're either trying to accuse me of being a white supremacist, too obsessed with the crusades, or a Christian trying to garner support. I honestly have no idea what you're trying to say, so I'm just gonna say this. Shalom Friend :D! I'm Jewish.

Once again, thank you for taking the time to look at my concept and review it. I appreciate you point out its flaws in an honest if not harsh manner, and I hope when I get this thing redesigned and more polished you'll come back to find something you can greenlight. If you have any other questions or concerns, feel free to tell me!

item.title: Re: Social Suicide: SCP Idea
item.content:encoded:
Hello Green05,
I'm going to preface by saying I am not a reviewer so take my word with a grain of salt. In any case, I actually think the idea is nice and simple (though that does leave the possibility of a similar object on the site). I think what will make or break the idea is the narrative direction you move in as there are lots of ways you could go. I think your concept usage as a weapon against high profile individuals is interesting and has potential. All that said, I have a few comments and questions to add:

Show More
Show Less

1. While the object is anomalous, I feel like the idea of it simultaneously erasing everyone's memory at once is a bit of a stretch. A possible idea is that maybe instead the object converts the person into a sort of anti-meme like the classic SCP-055. Any person observing the the individual will suffer memory loss relating to their existence.
2. Does this only affect memories up until the point of erasure, or can new memories not be made either?
3. How would this affect other indicators of their existence such as forms of media. If an individual was high profile, there would no doubt be textual or news media of their existence. How would that others reconcile with that knowledge?

I think you have something maybe potential here, but there are definitely some narrative and logistical loose ends that need to be ironed out first.

Regards,
VoxStulti
